properties.name: A REALIZES edge says whether anyone checked the artifact against what the target requires
properties.rationale: A real user found a real bug that every green signal in the design agreed was fine. That is the failure the served instructions warn about — a green gate is evidence about what it covers and silent about the rest — arriving from outside rather than from a detector. Anthony chose to make the absence first-class rather than merely documented, and required that the property ship with the report that reads it, so the count is the deliverable.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
Implements `dec:should-a-realizes-edge-say-that-nobody-checked-the-file-still-obeys-the-rule`, option (b), settled on Anthony's word 2026-08-16.

WHAT CHANGED. `REALIZES` gains `conformance: unchecked | reviewed | verified`, defaulting to `unchecked` (`schema/build.yaml`). `realizes()` and `link_artifact` take it; `ArtifactLink` returns what was stored. `DesignGraph::conformance_tally()` counts every realizing link by bucket and names up to ten unchecked ones, and `evidence_report` carries the tally so the number is reachable from the served surface.

⭐ THE MEASURED ANSWER ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN, taken end-to-end through a restarted server: 223 REALIZING LINKS, 223 UNCHECKED, 0 reviewed, 0 verified, 0 unrecognised. That sentence could not be produced at all before this change, and it is the entire deliverable — not the ceremony of setting a field, but the count that makes the silence visible.

WHY IT EXISTS, and the evidence came from OUTSIDE the project: a Requirement said the calendar day is the person's CIVIL date; the code used UTC; the Capability said `realized`; the artifact's checksum matched so `reconcile_artifacts` was silent. Every signal in the graph was green and A USER FOUND THE BUG IN THE PRODUCT. Nothing distinguished a file CHECKED AGAINST THE RULE from a file MERELY HASHED, and the two produced identical reports. Alex's Grok session, 2026-08-14, item 5.

WHY IT IS NOT A DETECTOR: reflow2 reads a DESIGN, never a running system, and judging whether code implements a civil-date rule is program analysis it deliberately stays out of (`dec:agent-navigates-content`). This RECORDS what a person knows; it computes nothing about code.

⭐ WHY (b) BEAT (a), documenting the hole — and this is the general principle rather than a preference: A DOCUMENTED HOLE IS SOMETHING A READER MUST REMEMBER; A DEFAULT OF `unchecked` IS SOMETHING THE GRAPH SAYS OUT LOUD EVERY TIME, WITH NOBODY REMEMBERING ANYTHING. The same move landed twice already this month and was right both times: #200 stopped INJECTING a default nobody chose, #213 started REPORTING the property nobody declared.

WHERE THE READER LIVES, and both alternatives were rejected for stated reasons. NOT `coverage_report`: it requires a caller-supplied file sweep, and making somebody sweep a tree to learn that nobody has checked anything puts a cost in front of the one number that should be free. NOT `loop_status`: every edge starts `unchecked`, so a large figure that never moves is exactly the signal-trained-to-be-ignored failure `req:the-loop-can-say-what-this-session-owes` was built to end — hours earlier, in this same session. `evidence_report` takes no arguments, is read on demand rather than nagged, and already speaks in this idiom.

DELIBERATE SHAPE:
- `conformance` DOES NOT FOLLOW `completeness` INTO OPTIMISM. `completeness` defaults to `complete`; conformance defaults to `unchecked`, because registering a file says it exists and never that anyone checked it.
- THE SAMPLE IS CAPPED AT TEN AND THE COUNT IS NOT. A truncated list that also truncated the count would under-report the problem, the one direction this must never fail in.
- A MISSING VALUE COUNTS AS `unchecked`, never as a separate unknown bucket — otherwise the number that matters shrinks for a reason that is not progress.
- AN UNRECOGNISED VALUE IS NAMED, not folded into a bucket: silently counting it as checked would be the flattering reading of an unreadable one.

⚠️ WHAT MUTATION TESTING TAUGHT, and it changed what could be tested. Mutating the fallback to report a missing conformance as `verified` killed only ONE case, which was suspicious — and the reason is that the schema `default:` MATERIALISES the property at write time. A probe confirmed it: a freshly written edge stores `conformance: "unchecked"` explicitly. So the in-code fallback covers ONLY edges written before the property existed, and that shape CANNOT be constructed through the API, because a property once written cannot be removed (`fact:defect-a-property-once-written-cannot-be-removed`, found earlier the same day). It is therefore proven against the real graph rather than in a unit test — all 223 links predate the property and all 223 report `unchecked`.

VERIFIED. 11 cases, all passing. Three mutations, each killing the right case: capping the count as well as the sample; defaulting link_artifact to optimism; and the fallback mutation above, whose partial kill was itself the finding. Two counterweights pin the distinction that defines the feature — a COMPLETE artifact is still unchecked, and a MATCHING CHECKSUM is still unchecked, which is precisely the shipped-bug case: complete, hashed, green, wrong.

NO SCHEMA STAMP MOVEMENT: an edge PROPERTY is not counted by the version stamp — 29 node types, 61 edge types, unchanged — so no upgrade document is owed.

NOT DONE, named rather than left to be discovered. Nothing MOVES an edge off `unchecked` except a caller saying so, and nothing forces that; the honest claim is that the silence is now countable, not that it will be broken. Option (d), raising unchecked links as a gap, is deliberately deferred — 223 gaps on day one is noise, and it costs almost nothing later because the data now exists. And the 223 are not triaged here; this change measures them, it does not fix them.
